\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{كشف} (kashafa)}{كشف (kashafa)}]{\ar{كشف} (kashafa) — to uncover, to reveal}

\label{lesson:AR-C312-kashafa}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to have a child, then the Arabic for a naming.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{كشف}}
\textbf{\ar{كشف}} — \emph{kashafa} — \textquotedblleft{}to uncover, to reveal\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{كشف} \ar{التحقيق} \ar{سبب} \ar{الحريق}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{kashafa at-taḥqīq sabab al-ḥarīq.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The investigation revealed the cause of the fire.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يكشف}, \emph{yakshif}.

\ar{كشف} \ar{عن}: to disclose. A medical check-up is \ar{كشف} \ar{طبي}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{كشف}} (\emph{kashafa}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{k-sh-f} (Lane), \textquotedblleft{}to take away a covering from a thing\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kashafa}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kashafa}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kashafa at-taḥqīq sabab al-ḥarīq.} — The investigation revealed the cause of the fire.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to have a child, then the Arabic for a naming, then say \emph{kashafa} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{كشف} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To uncover, to reveal\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{اكتشف} (iktashafa)}{اكتشف (iktashafa)}]{\ar{اكتشف} (iktashafa) — to discover}

\label{lesson:AR-C312-iktashafa}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a naming, then the Arabic for to uncover.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{اكتشف}}
\textbf{\ar{اكتشف}} — \emph{iktashafa} — \textquotedblleft{}to discover\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{اكتشف} \ar{العلماء} \ar{نجما} \ar{جديدا}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{iktashafa al-ʿulamāʾ najman jadīdan.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The scientists discovered a new star.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يكتشف}, \emph{yaktashif}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{اكتشف}} (\emph{iktashafa}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{k-sh-f} (Lane), \textquotedblleft{}to uncover\textquotedblright{}. It is Form VIII, \textquotedblleft{}to uncover for oneself\textquotedblright{}: to find out.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{عثر} (ʿathara)}{عثر (ʿathara)}]{\ar{عثر} (ʿathara) — to come across, to find}

\label{lesson:AR-C312-athara-find}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to uncover, then the Arabic for to discover.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{عثر}}
\textbf{\ar{عثر}} — \emph{ʿathara} — \textquotedblleft{}to come across, to find\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{عثر} \ar{الولد} \ar{على} \ar{مفتاح} \ar{في} \ar{الحديقة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ʿathara al-walad ʿalā miftāḥ fī al-ḥadīqa.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The boy came across a key in the garden.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يعثر}, \emph{yaʿthur}.

It takes \ar{على}: \ar{عثر} \ar{على}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{عثر}} (\emph{ʿathara}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ʿ-th-r} (Lane), \textquotedblleft{}to stumble\textquotedblright{}, the root of the taught \emph{taʿaththara}. To stumble upon a thing is to find it.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{مستكشف} (mustakshif)}{مستكشف (mustakshif)}]{\ar{مستكشف} (mustakshif) — an explorer}

\label{lesson:AR-C312-mustakshif}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to discover, then the Arabic for to come across.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{مستكشف}}
\textbf{\ar{مستكشف}} — \emph{mustakshif} — \textquotedblleft{}an explorer\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{عبر} \ar{المستكشف} \ar{الصحراء} \ar{على} \ar{جمل}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ʿabara al-mustakshif aṣ-ṣaḥrāʾ ʿalā jamal.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The explorer crossed the desert on a camel.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{مستكشف}} (\emph{mustakshif}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{k-sh-f} (Lane), \textquotedblleft{}to uncover\textquotedblright{}. \emph{Mustakshif} is the Form X participle, \textquotedblleft{}one who seeks to uncover\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{كنز} (kanz)}{كنز (kanz)}]{\ar{كنز} (kanz) — a treasure}

\label{lesson:AR-C312-kanz}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to come across, then the Arabic for an explorer.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{كنز}}
\textbf{\ar{كنز}} — \emph{kanz} — \textquotedblleft{}a treasure\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{وجد} \ar{الصياد} \ar{كنزا} \ar{تحت} \ar{الرمل}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{wajada aṣ-ṣayyād kanzan taḥta ar-raml.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The fisherman found a treasure under the sand.
\end{quote}

Plural: \ar{كنوز}, \emph{kunūz}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{كنز}} (\emph{kanz}) is built on the root \emph{k-n-z}, \textquotedblleft{}to store up, to bury wealth\textquotedblright{} (Lane). A link with Persian \emph{ganj}, treasure, is often proposed, but the origin is not settled.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}
